summary: A technical security review focused on ensuring Redwood can support strict EU data residency and region pinning for Aurelia Health's PHI workloads. Discussed region pinning options (hosted EU-only tenancy, Dedicated, Private/VPC), cross-border processing, KMS/encryption, audit logs, SSO/RBAC controls, and sub-processor disclosures. Agreed next steps include sharing architecture diagrams, compliance pack, and scheduling a scoped POC for EU-only tenancy.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Carlos Martinez (CISO, Aurelia Health), Anne Wu (Head of Platform, Aurelia), Liam O'Connor (Legal)
Shared items: compliance_pack_v2.pdf (link), EU-region-arch.png (link), subprocessor_list.xlsx (link)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, can you hear me?
[00:05] Carlos Martinez: Yep, loud and clear. Thank you.
[00:08] Anne Wu: Hi all.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan here. I'll be taking the technical side.

[00:30] Maya: Super. The goal for today is to walk through how Redwood handles data residency and region pinning, answer questions around cross-border processing, KMS, and sub-processors, and then map to your PHI requirements. Carlos, do you want to kick off with your main requirements?
[00:45] Carlos: Sure. Our core ask is that certain workloads stay in the EU — processing and storage — we can't have tokens or logs leaving the EU for those. We also need visibility into sub-processors and proof of contractual restrictions. And obviously audit logs at the tenant level.
[01:10] Maya: Got it. Jordan, quick overview on deployment options?
[01:15] Jordan: Yeah. There are three common patterns we recommend: hosted EU-only tenancy where requests and persistence remain in EU regions; Dedicated — reserved GPU pools in EU that we can pin; and Private (VPC/on-prem) for full control. For EU-only hosted, we do region pinning at the routing layer and control storage and backups to EU regions. For Dedicated, we reserve capacity in EU data centers. For Private, customer-managed network and keys.
[01:48] Anne: How deterministic is the routing? Our compliance folks want to ensure there's no accidental failover to the US.
[01:55] Jordan: Good question. We have policy-based routing with strict pinning flags. If you mark a tenant or route as EU-pinned, the runtime will only route to EU-backed pools. We do have automatic fallback policies for availability, but for pinned tenants we can disable cross-region fallback. There is a tradeoff — higher availability requires multi-region coverage, which can introduce cross-border movement unless you use Dedicated/Private.
[02:30] Carlos: So for PHI we can't accept cross-border fallback. That means Dedicated or Private for these workloads?
[02:36] Jordan: Typically yes. Hosted EU-only tenancy can be configured to avoid cross-border, but we recommend Dedicated or Private for strict legal controls and SLAs. Note: our hosted offering can be contractually restricted, and we can provide SOC 2 / ISO extracts.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: On KMS — we need customer-controlled keys that never leave the EU region. Is that available?
[03:05] Jordan: We support customer-managed KMS. For hosted EU tenancy we can integrate with your cloud KMS in-region; keys are stored and wrapped in EU. For Private deployments you manage KMS entirely. There's a nuance: some metadata like routing headers are non-PHI and may transit control planes, we can document which pieces are global.
[03:32] Carlos: That metadata bit worries us — what exactly transits the control plane? Even pseudonymous IDs?
[03:38] Jordan: Good flag. The control plane holds non-content metadata: request routing IDs, billing pointers, and tenant config. Content and KV caches are kept in-region when pinned. That said, our security pack notes which logs are global versus region-local — we'll highlight that in the doc we share.
[03:58] Maya: We'll attach the compliance pack and the EU-region-arch diagram after the call.

[04:20] Anne: Sub-processors — can you share a list and do you have EU-based partners? We need to run them through our vendor program.
[04:28] Jordan: Yes, we have a current sub-processor list; most infra partners in EU are local cloud providers and storage subs. We'll share the spreadsheet. We also support contractual addenda for data processing terms and will accept certain negotiation points on subprocessors.
[04:47] Carlos: Are backups geo-replicated? We need backups to stay in EU and retention policies to be configurable.
[04:53] Jordan: Backups can be configured per-tenant to remain in EU, and retention is configurable. Default hosted may replicate for durability, but for pinned tenants we ensure EU-only replication. There can be a small ops window for metadata, again we'll call that out.

[05:20] Liam: For audit logs and e-discovery — how granular? We need tenant-level logs with request IDs, user IDs, and exportable for legal hold. Also chain-of-custody.
[05:30] Jordan: We provide audit logs with configurable retention. Logs include request IDs, caller principal, model used, and tokens metadata. We can export logs to your SIEM in-region (e.g., EU Splunk or S3) and support signed exports for chain-of-custody. We'll outline the fields in the pack.
[05:55] Carlos: Is there any chance PII or content is included in these logs by default?
[06:00] Jordan: By default content is not logged; we log metadata and hashes. If you enable full request logging for debugging, that's opt-in and can be configured to stay in-region and encrypted with your keys.

[06:22] Anne: On SSO and RBAC — we use SAML SSO and want SCIM to provision groups. Can you map to our groups and enforce tenant-level RBAC?
[06:30] Maya: Yes, we support SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and tenant-level RBAC. Jordan can speak to enforcement in runtime.
[06:37] Jordan: RBAC is enforced at the control plane and runtime with tokens scoped by tenant and role. SCIM sync can create groups and roles. We do periodic token rotation and session tracing. There are some transients in session tokens but those are short-lived and can be bound to IP ranges in VPC/Private setups.

[07:05] Carlos: A question on sub-processors again — do you use any US-based telemetry providers that might receive telemetry even if content is EU-bound?
[07:12] Jordan: We avoid sending telemetry with content to US-based analytics for pinned tenants. Some global health metrics (aggregated, non-PII) may be sent to a global telemetry pipeline, but we can opt you out for EU-pinned tenants. We'll mark that in the sub-processor sheet.
[07:35] Anne: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts that show the controls around region pinning and KMS?
[07:42] Maya: Yes — we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 summaries. We'll extract the sections relevant to data residency and key management and include them in the pack.

[08:05] Liam: Regarding contractual language — will Redwood accept EU data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses where needed?
[08:12] Maya: We provide a DPA with SCCs as required and can include EU-specific clauses in enterprise amendments. Our legal team is used to these asks for healthcare customers.

[08:30] Carlos: Operationally, we want to run a small POC: bring a representative dataset (anonymized PHI), route it through an EU-pinned tenant, and verify logs, backups, and key residency. How quickly can that be set up?
[08:44] Jordan: We can provision an EU-pinned hosted tenancy for a POC in about 3-5 business days. If you require Dedicated, that adds provisioning lead time — typically 2-3 weeks depending on capacity. Private deployments are longer. For the POC we recommend hosted EU-pinned with customer KMS integration.
[09:05] Anne: For the POC, can we get SIEM export hooks and the audit logs shipped to our EU Splunk instance?
[09:12] Jordan: Yes, we can set up export connectors and will work with your Splunk team on the integration.

[09:40] Maya: Quick note — there was a past mention of KV cache being global in an earlier doc; that's incorrect for pinned tenants. There's a legacy doc where "KV cash" was mentioned, we'll correct that.
[09:52] Carlos: (laughs) That's fine.

[10:05] Jordan: One more nuance on cross-border processing: if you use third-party models or marketplace models that we can't host EU-local due to licensing, that could cause cross-border calls. For strict residency you should pin to our curated EU-verify models or bring your own model in Private.
[10:30] Anne: Good point. We'll stick to curated models.

[11:00] Liam: On encryption in transit — TLS everywhere is standard, but do you support mTLS between services inside the region?
[11:07] Jordan: Yes, we use mutual TLS for internal service-to-service comms in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we rely on TLS with strong ciphers and we can provide cert chain details.

[11:35] Carlos: Is there any residual metadata that would be considered personal data under GDPR and might leave the region?
[11:42] Jordan: The main items are request timestamps and tenant IDs which could be linked to a user. We can minimize retention and ensure those fields are pseudonymized or kept only in-region. We'll call out exact fields in the pack.

[12:05] Maya: Quick check — any blockers so far for a POC?
[12:10] Carlos: No blockers, just need the sub-processor list, SOC extracts, and the EU-arch diagram. Also need contractual language from Legal for DPA/SCC.
[12:20] Liam: We will review DPA drafts.

[12:36] Jordan: I'll draft the EU-pinning architecture and point out which services are in-region vs global control plane.
[12:44] Maya: I'll send the compliance pack and schedule the POC kickoff next week.

[13:00] Anne: One practical question — how do you handle geo based DNS and latency routing? We need low latency for inferencing.
[13:08] Jordan: For EU-only tenants we use region-local ingress and an edge layer in EU. We can also stand up Dedicated pools in specific EU zones. Latency is typical 20-80ms depending on model and region. We'll provide benchmark numbers.

[13:45] Carlos: Any special considerations for e-discovery or legal holds where we might need to freeze data?
[13:50] Jordan: We support legal hold at the tenant level — you can freeze deletion and extract a snapshot. Snapshots are stored in-region. We'll document the process and the chain-of-custody steps.

[14:10] Liam: On the sub-processor spreadsheet, will you highlight which vendors have EU data centers?
[14:14] Jordan: Yes, we'll annotate the list.

[14:35] Maya: OK let's recap and assign owners. Action items and next steps will be emailed. Anything else?
[14:42] Carlos: Nothing from my side. Thanks.
[14:45] Anne: All good.
[14:48] Liam: Thanks everyone.

[14:55] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and proposed POC dates.

End notes: meeting ran ~42 minutes. Shared artifacts will include: compliance_pack_v2.pdf, EU-region-arch.png, subprocessor_list.xlsx. Next steps reiterated in metadata above.
